findings.message: examples/flashlight/run_orbit_workflow.sh:177-198 always injects --disable-render-history and then appends extra user args. Because examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py:103-105 defines --disable-render-history and --enable-render-history as mutually exclusive, the documented helper override `examples/flashlight/run_orbit_workflow.sh render -- --enable-render-history` fails at argparse with `argument --enable-render-history: not allowed with argument --disable-render-history`. Either omit the helper's explicit disable flag because the Python default is already disabled, or add a real helper flag/env var that chooses exactly one render-history option. The docs at examples/flashlight/README.md:242-245 and docs/running_our_example_applications.md:173-177 should match the resulting helper semantics.

Core render-loop behavior looks correct: examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py:994-998 marks each component's bCameraCutThisFrame before CaptureScene, and examples/flashlight/run_orbit_collection.py:1455-1457 calls it after camera/light pose updates inside each explicit frame capture.

The tests are meaningful for the focused change: they cover default disabled render history, explicit enable/disable parse behavior, camera-cut assignment at capture time, scene-light grouping, scene-off arg isolation, and validation of the checked-in light-settings trio.

follow_up_recommendations: Fix the workflow helper override path for --enable-render-history and add a lightweight shell or subprocess test for that helper behavior.
Run a short live simulator scene_off_flashlight_on orbit smoke test when a simulator session is available to visually confirm brightness stability.
